This was the highest December-to-December increase since 1981. Specifically, food prices increased by 6.3% and food at home prices by 6.5%.

related_questions.title: November Inflation Report: Price Gains Slow More Than Expected

text_blocks.snippet: In November 2021, U.S. inflation surged to a 39-year high, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising 6.8% compared to the previous year. This was the fastest pace since 1982. The core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, increased by 4.9% year-over-year, marking the fastest increase since 1991.
snippet_highlighted_words: U.S. inflation surged to a 39-year high

text_blocks.snippet: Several factors contributed to this surge in inflation:

list.title: Increased Demand:
list.snippet: Strong consumer demand, particularly for durable goods like autos and appliances, outpaced supply, leading to price increases.

list.title: Supply Chain Issues:
list.snippet: Disruptions in the global supply chain, exacerbated by the ongoing pandemic, created shortages of goods and drove up prices.

list.title: Labor Shortages:
list.snippet: Businesses struggled to find enough workers, leading to wage increases that were often passed on to consumers through higher prices.

list.title: Rising Energy Costs:
list.snippet: Energy prices, including gasoline and fuel oil, saw significant increases, contributing to the overall inflation rate.

text_blocks.snippet: The Federal Reserve was expected to respond to the rising inflation by accelerating the tapering of its bond-buying stimulus program, paving the way for potential interest rate hikes as early as March 2022.
